name: Tide Clock
description: The tide at a place: a classic tide-clock dial with one hand sweeping from high water through low and back, the tide curve for the next day or two with now marked, today's highs and lows with times and heights, sunrise and sunset on the curve, and the Moon's phase. Open-Meteo's marine model anywhere on the coast with no key, or a NOAA station's exact predictions in the United States.

cell_options.name: location
cell_options.label: Place
cell_options.help: The shore whose tide to show. Sunrise, sunset and the clock are read here too. Falls back to the app-level location in Settings when empty.

cell_options.name: source
cell_options.label: Source
cell_options.help: Open-Meteo's marine model gives a modelled coastal sea level anywhere in the world with no key. It is an ocean model, not a harbour tide table, and can be an hour or so out and a little short in estuaries and bays. A NOAA station gives the exact published predictions for a tide station in the United States.

cell_options.name: station
cell_options.label: NOAA station
cell_options.help: The seven-digit station id, for example 9414290 for San Francisco. Find yours at https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/ under Tide Predictions. Heights are above MLLW, as NOAA publishes them.

cell_options.name: layout
cell_options.label: Layout
cell_options.help: Dial and curve puts the clock beside the curve and today's list. Almanac is the curve alone under a headline, with sunrise, sunset and the Moon. Dial is the clock on its own with the next turn of the tide beneath it, for a small cell.

cell_options.name: hours
cell_options.label: Curve
cell_options.help: How far the curve runs. It starts a few hours before now so the last turn of the tide stays in view.
